cards.text: Ezekiel, a prophet, is in the middle of a vision of a temple, and he's telling it himself. A man with a measuring rod (Ezekiel 40:3) has been walking him all over it, wall after wall after WALL (Ezekiel 40:5-42:20), and friend, I stamp cookies for a living and even I'd have asked for a cookie break. Now the man brings Ezekiel back to the gate that faces east.

cards.question: Ezekiel is standing at the gate that faces east when he sees the glory of the God of Israel coming. Which direction is it coming from?

cards.text: His voice is like the roar of many waters, and the earth shines with His glory. Friend, the brightest thing in my old junk drawer was a birthday candle somebody used once.

Ezekiel says this vision is like the one he saw when God came to destroy the city, and like the visions he saw by the River Kebar, so he knows EXACTLY what he's looking at. Me? I spent years in a junk drawer and still couldn't tell a dead battery from a good one.

cards.question: Standing before the glory of the God of Israel, Ezekiel falls ___.
With Ezekiel facedown, the glory of the LORD enters the temple through the gate facing east. True or false?

cards.text: Then the Spirit lifts Ezekiel up and brings him into the inner court. Me? I hop everywhere I go, base and all, and I STILL show up out of breath.

cards.question: Ezekiel is in the inner court now, and the ___ of the LORD fills the temple.

cards.text: The man is still standing right beside Ezekiel, so it's not him talking. Someone is speaking to Ezekiel from INSIDE the temple, and friend, that's the moment you put your phone face down and LISTEN.

cards.question: From inside the temple, God calls Ezekiel son of man and says this is the place of His throne and the place for the soles of His feet. What does He say He will do there?

answers.text: Rule from there for a season
Judge the nations one last time

cards.text: He says Israel and their kings will never again defile His holy name. Back then, they put their threshold right next to His with only a wall between Him and them, and friend, that's not a neighbor, that's a ROOMMATE.

cards.question: God says that when they built right up against His temple, He overlooked the abominations they committed. True or false?

cards.text: No overlooking: God says He consumed them in His anger. Now He says to let them remove their prostitution and the funeral offerings for their kings far from Him, and He will dwell among them forever, that promise AGAIN.

cards.question: Israel defiled God's holy name right next door to Him. Now God tells Ezekiel to describe the holy temple to them, so that they may be ___ of their iniquities.
If Israel is ashamed of all they've done, God tells Ezekiel to write the temple's design down where they can see it. True or false?
Then God gives Ezekiel the law of the temple. What does it say about all the temple's surrounding territory on top of the mountain?

answers.text: It will belong to the king
It will be open for trade

cards.text: Then God gives the altar's measurements in long cubits: a gutter at the base, ledges stepping up, a square hearth twelve cubits each way with four horns, and steps facing east. Friend, I measure chocolate chips by the mustache-full.

Then the Lord GOD gives the statutes for the altar's first days, served by the Levitical priests from the family of Zadok, a priest in King David's day (2 Samuel 8:17): seven days of sin offerings and burnt offerings, blood on the altar's horns and salt on the burnt offerings, until the altar is cleansed and consecrated. SEVEN days just to get the altar ready, friend, and I complain when my oven takes ten minutes to preheat.

cards.question: After seven days of atonement, from the eighth day on, the priests present burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar. What does the Lord GOD say He will do then?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Keep your apron on, because this vision is NOT done yet.

findings.problem: The question calls it "the holy temple," but Ezekiel 43:10 only says "describe the temple." The added word also hints at the answer to card 16, which asks what the law of the temple says about its territory ("most holy"). Drop "holy."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "Describe the holy temple" changes the text's wording. Ezekiel 43:10 says "describe the temple."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "So he knows EXACTLY what he's looking at" goes beyond the text. Ezekiel 43:3 only says the vision was like his earlier visions. It never says what Ezekiel concluded or knew. Either mark it as Papa Dorin's guess or drop it.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't make sense. The core action is enduring a long, tiring tour, but "I stamp cookies for a living and even I'd have asked for a cookie break" doesn't share that action. Nothing explains why stamping cookies would make him better at enduring it. A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action. ... If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Card 20 is only the "story isn't over" line, which the rules allow when the last verse was asked on a choice card. It tells nothing from any verse, yet it cites Ezekiel 43:27. The citation rule says a story card cites exactly the verses it tells, but the docs don't say what a story card that tells no verse should cite.
findings.question: What should the verses field be for a closing story card that is only the "story isn't over" line: the last verse of the passage, the verse of the choice card before it, or something else?
